name: Paludal-Minaret
description: Glacier upon glacier, blue-white and creaking, buried in places by nitrogen snow. The shell is broken in places by an orbital debris ring, and through those breaches the deep ocean breathes plumes of frost into the dark.
No wind, no voice, no weather: the landscape communicates in light and shadow alone, and it has plenty to say at sunrise.
Local legend among spacers says the planet hums on a frequency just below hearing. Instruments confirm it. Nobody agrees on the source.
Mining charters include clauses about 'subsurface events' that lawyers refuse to define.
